A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PPLLaVA and retain matching core equations, experiments, and examples. Their complete text and visual material are readable, including v3 Appendices A–C and the corresponding qualitative and limitations sections in v1. Some experimental settings are less explicit in v3, but this does not prevent reliable comparison of the documents.

before.justification: V1 reports original PPLLaVA benchmark results, throughput measurements, component and training ablations, and qualitative outputs in Tables 1–9 and Figures 3–7.

after.justification: V3 reports original results for three PPLLaVA backbone configurations, token-budget comparisons, ablations, and attention visualizations, including material in Appendix A.

M1.justification: The three core modules and Equations 1–4 remain unchanged. V3 adds an InternVL3-specific contrastive realignment stage using CLIP-L14-text with frozen InternViT-300M, and no longer includes v1's optional DPO stage in the reported training pipeline. These are limited initialization and auxiliary-training changes to the retained pooling method.

E1.justification: V3 removes MSVD-QA and MSRVTT-QA evaluation, adds EgoSchema and LongVideoBench, and evaluates NExT-QA, which already appeared as training data in v1. This broadens egocentric and long-video reasoning evaluation while reducing open-ended QA coverage. V3 also introduces LAION and Wukong image–text data for encoder alignment. The image benchmark suite is retained.

E2.justification: V3 Table 2 adds comparators such as LLaVA-OneVision, LLaVA-Video, InternVL3, and VideoLLaMA2/3 on retained video benchmarks. Earlier ActivityNet/VCG comparisons against BT-Adapter, Vista-LLaMA, and VLM-RLAIF are removed. V3 Table 5 also adds a ToME-like token-merging comparator to the retained pooling comparison.

E3.justification: V3 adds backbone configurations spanning 7B/8B models, a comparison at matched visual-token budgets, and a 10M-pair alignment-training stage. The reported instruction-data total changes from 1.36M to 1.16M, and v1's stated 760k comparison exception disappears. These are reported setting changes; the PDFs do not establish which retained experiments were rerun. V3's main VideoMME table also leaves subtitle conditions unspecified.

E4.justification: V3 adds the token-budget comparison in Figure 1(b), a token-merging alternative in Table 5, and generic-prompt attention analysis in Figure 6 and Appendix A. It removes v1's dedicated frame-count/kernel experiment and modality-interleaving/DPO ablation in Tables 8–9. The component ablation and spatial/temporal pooling sensitivity curves are retained.

E5.justification: Neither PDF reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or statistical error bars. The quantitative tables and performance curves continue to present point estimates.

E6.justification: V3 adds extensive results for new configurations and benchmarks: Table 2 reports VideoMME overall scores of 64.5 and 67.1 for the LLaVA-Video and InternVL3 variants, and Table 5 adds token merging at 51.9 with 2048 tokens. These are newly reported settings, not demonstrated same-setting gains over v1. MSVD/MSRVTT results, DPO results, and MVBench task-level breakdowns disappear. The reported PLLaVA VCG score also changes from 2.99 to 3.12.

T1.justification: The certificate construction and mathematical definitions of alignment weights, pooling dimensions, weighted aggregation, and positional interpolation are retained. Equations 1–4 change only in presentation. Appendix B's new Q-Former analogy supplies conceptual motivation, without adding formal assumptions, propositions, or proofs.

C1.justification: V1 frames the central problem as achieving unified short- and long-video understanding through image-model transfer. V3 instead emphasizes reducing the computational cost of already capable long-context MLLMs and explicitly claims generalization across image, video, and general-purpose backbones with different encoders. The abstract and introduction drop the highlighted DPO/codebase contribution and introduce matched-token efficiency claims.

C2.justification: V3 introduces a learned-feature explanation for performance with uninformative prompts and adds substantive prompt-dependence and context-length limitations in Appendix B. It removes v1's discussion of the multi-image/dialogue tradeoff and DPO's hallucination benefits. Section 4.2 also newly attributes advantages to motion priors, although the described method does not identify a corresponding component.

D1.justification: V3 adds encoder-specific alignment and initialization details and newly specifies video-only training for ablations. Reported full-training time changes from 24 to 36 hours. It removes v1's repository link and the statement that both questions and answers enter CLIP during training. These are substantial documentation changes; the omissions do not establish that the repository became unavailable or that training inputs changed.

R1.justification: V3 substantially expands positioning around modern unified MLLMs, long-context compression, and key-content extraction, citing works such as Qwen2.5-VL, InternVL3, LongVA, Video-XL, LongVU, VideoAgent, and VideoTree. A new Key Content Extraction discussion distinguishes PPLLaVA from iterative frame-search methods. V1's DPO/RLHF positioning and associated references are removed.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, main-results narrative, and conclusion are extensively rewritten around efficiency and backbone generalization. Separate benchmark discussions are consolidated, and qualitative results and limitations move into appendices. Author information and publication headers also change. This is substantial narrative restructuring beyond the addition of experiments.

P2.justification: Figure 1(b)'s radar chart is replaced by a token-count/performance plot. V1's detailed video benchmark tables are reorganized into v3's consolidated Table 2, and the frame-count and training-ablation tables disappear. V3 adds the generic-prompt attention montage and relocates retained qualitative figures into Appendix A; v1 Figure 6 becomes v3 Figure 8. Figure 2 also gains explanatory arrow labels.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's single-backbone evidence, v3 strengthens the central efficiency and generalization argument through the matched-token comparison in Figure 1(b) and three-backbone evaluation in Table 2. The new prompt-dependence discussion and visualizations clarify an important applicability boundary. These gains are tempered by lost interleaving analysis, removal of the repository link, less explicit VideoMME subtitle conditions, and the unexplained motion-priors attribution. The net quality improvement is therefore limited.
